newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka army cracks down on deserters.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka army cracks down on deserters.

text.p: Sri Lanka's military, battling Tamil Tiger separatists in the north and east, on Thursday announced a crackdown on deserters.
"Deserters will be court-martialled when they are arrested," military spokesman Brigadier Sarath Munasinghe told a news conference in Colombo.

He said in one of the first examples of the stricter penalties, a soldier on Thursday was given three years' rigorous imprisonment for deserting his post in the war against the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE).
Three other soldiers were also facing court-martial.
The desertion rate in Sri Lankan forces, especially police and paramilitary manning northern defences, is said to be high although no confirmed figures are available.
The government last year announced an amnesty for deserters and said those who returned would not be punished. It also said those employing army deserters would be prosecuted.
Goverment troops have been fighting the LTTE, who are demanding an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east, since 1983.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war. The LTTE say the toll is higher.

Casualties on both sides have been high this year after some 20,000 troops launched Operation Jaya Sikuru, or Sure of Victory, to open a strategic highway through the brush jungles of the Wanni region, linking northern Jaffna peninsula with the rest of the island.
